brief: JPMorgan enters 3Q26 semis earnings season constructive but selective. YTD outperformance (SMH +68%) stems from AI infrastructure investment, supply tightness, and a broadening non-AI cyclical recovery, so JPM expects focus to shift from already-understood demand to supply constraints and how fast capacity can relieve them. Dynamics diverge by subsector, so JPM stays selective. Top picks are AVGO and MRVL, with NVDA, AMD, MU, SNDK, TXN, ADI, AMAT, LRCX, and KLAC also highlighted. In AI compute, supply (foundry, HBM, packaging, power), not demand, gates growth, pushing custom XPU share of accelerator units from about 32% in CY25 toward about 53% in CY27E and favoring AVGO and MRVL. Networking is framed as the fastest-growing AI-stack layer. In memory, structural shortage deepens through CY28 as Micron's SCA/LTA contracts lock over 75% of FY27 output and reset HBM pricing higher, which JPM argues should drive a sector re-rating despite YTD gains. In semicap, WFE growth decelerates from 31% in 2026 to 38% in 2027 then 17% in 2028, with the debate being whether cleanroom capacity, not demand, caps revenue conversion. JPM prefers KLAC on 2027 leverage. Auto stays cautious on falling vehicle production. Industrial and analog look cleaner on content gains and pricing.
